description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved, comforting Turkish red lentil soup, known for its vibrant color and rich, savory flavor. This hearty soup is a staple in Turkish homes, offering a nourishing and delicious meal perfect for any time of year. Its smooth texture and aromatic spices make it an irresistible classic.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Vegetables
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Drain well. Finely chop the onion and dice the carrot. Set aside.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and saute for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the diced carrot and cook for another 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.

instructions.title: Add Tomato Paste and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to combine with the vegetables and tomato paste.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the hot water or vegetable broth. Add salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and carrots are very soft.

instructions.title: Blend to Smoothness
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches a smooth, creamy consistency. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Adjust seasoning if needed.

instructions.title: Prepare and Add the Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber) and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices. Pour this spiced butter directly over the blended soup.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Stir the spiced butter topping into the soup or drizzle it on top of individual servings. Serve the Mercimek Corbasi hot, garnished with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice from lemon wedges if desired. Enjoy with crusty bread.

tips: For extra depth of flavor, roast the carrots and onions slightly before adding them to the pot.
Do not skip the lemon juice when serving; it truly brightens the soup and is a signature Turkish touch.
Leftover Mercimek Corbasi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. It thickens as it cools, so you may need to add a splash of water or broth when reheating.
article:
## Mercimek Corbasi: The Soul-Warming Embrace of Turkish Red Lentil Soup

In the heart of Turkish cuisine lies a warmth that transcends geographical boundaries and culinary preferences. Among the myriad of delightful dishes, one stands out as a true staple, a comforting embrace in a bowl: Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, creamy, and incredibly flavorful soup is more than just a dish; it's a taste of home for millions, a culinary hug that nourishes both body and soul. Whether served as a hearty breakfast, a light lunch, or the perfect start to a traditional Turkish feast, Mercimek Corbasi embodies the simplicity and richness of Turkish cooking. Its humble ingredients transform into a symphony of flavors, making it a favorite across all generations.

## What is Turkish Red Lentil Soup (Mercimek Corbasi)?

Mercimek Corbasi, literally translating to "lentil soup," is a quintessential Turkish dish renowned for its distinctive red-orange hue, silky smooth texture, and deeply savory taste. Unlike some lentil soups that might feature whole lentils, the hallmark of Mercimek Corbasi is its velvety consistency, achieved by blending the cooked red lentils until perfectly smooth. It’s a soup that manages to be both incredibly light and surprisingly filling, packed with plant-based protein and fiber, making it a nutritious choice any time of day.

This iconic soup is a testament to the Turkish philosophy of using fresh, simple ingredients to create profound flavors. It’s a dish that evokes memories of bustling bazaars, cozy family kitchens, and the generous hospitality for which Turkey is famous. While variations exist across regions, the core essence of this Turkish Red Lentil Soup remains consistent: a comforting, wholesome, and utterly delicious experience that has captivated palates for centuries.

## Ingredients for Authentic Mercimek Corbasi

Creating an authentic bowl of Mercimek Corbasi requires a handful of accessible ingredients that, when combined, produce its signature taste. The beauty lies in their quality and the way they are brought together.

Here are the key components you'll need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. These quick-cooking lentils break down beautifully to create the soup's creamy texture. Ensure they are thoroughly rinsed before use.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic foundation. Finely chopped, they provide a sweet and pungent base.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** Essential for depth of flavor and that characteristic reddish color. Good quality Turkish tomato paste makes a significant difference.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** A crucial herb that lends a unique, refreshing, and distinctly Turkish flavor. Don't skip it!
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber):** Adds a gentle warmth and a beautiful visual appeal. Adjust to your spice preference.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** Used for sautéing the aromatics and creating the flavorful topping.
*   **Vegetable or Chicken Broth/Water:** The liquid base. Broth adds more richness, but water works perfectly well, especially if you're aiming for a lighter soup.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season and enhance all the flavors.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Absolutely essential for serving, adding a bright, tangy finish.

## Step-by-Step: How to Make Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Making Mercimek Corbasi is a straightforward process, even for beginner cooks. Follow these steps to create your own delicious Turkish Red Lentil Soup:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse 1 cup of red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any dust or impurities.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add 1 finely chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 2 cloves of minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
3.  **Build the Flavor Base:** Stir in 1 tablespoon of tomato paste and cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, allowing it to deepen in color and flavor. Add 1 teaspoon of dried mint and 1/2 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (or more to taste), stirring for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
4.  **Add Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the aromatic mixture. Pour in 6 cups of vegetable or chicken broth (or water). Season with 1 teaspoon of salt and 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper.
5.  **Simmer and Cook:** Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6.  **Blend to Perfection:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot broth or water until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
7.  **Prepare the Topping (Optional but Recommended):** In a small pan, melt 1 tablespoon of butter (or olive oil) over medium heat. Add 1/2 teaspoon of dried mint and 1/4 teaspoon of red pepper flakes. Sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Turkish Red Lentil Soup into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the spiced butter topping over each serving and garnish with fresh lemon wedges.

## Pro Tips for the Best Mercimek Corbasi

Achieving that perfect, restaurant-quality Mercimek Corbasi is easier with a few expert tips:

*   **Rinse Thoroughly:** Don't underestimate the importance of rinsing your red lentils. It helps remove starch and ensures a cleaner flavor.
*   **Bloom Your Spices:** Cooking the tomato paste, dried mint, and red pepper flakes briefly in oil before adding the liquid "blooms" them, intensifying their flavors and aromas.
*   **Blend Until Silky:** For that signature creamy texture, blend the soup until it's absolutely smooth. No chunky bits should remain. An immersion blender makes this incredibly easy.
*   **The Lemon is Key:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end brightens the entire soup, cutting through the richness and adding a crucial tangy note. It's non-negotiable for an authentic experience.
*   **Don't Skip the Topping:** While optional, the spiced butter (or olive oil) drizzle, often called *nane yağı* (mint oil) or *salçalı sos* (tomato paste sauce), adds an extra layer of flavor and a beautiful visual flourish that elevates the soup from good to extraordinary.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Red Lentil Soup

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways:

*   **With Crusty Bread:** A thick slice of fresh, crusty bread (like Turkish pide or a simple baguette) is perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the soup.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Always serve with plenty of lemon wedges on the side for individual customization.
*   **As a Starter:** It makes an excellent appetizer for any meal, especially a traditional Turkish spread featuring kebabs, mezes, and rice pilaf.
*   **Light Meal:** Paired with a simple salad, Mercimek Corbasi can be a satisfying and healthy light lunch or dinner.
*   **Garnishes:** A sprinkle of fresh parsley or a dollop of plain yogurt can add extra freshness and creaminess, though traditionally, the soup is often served simply with the lemon and spiced oil.

## Variations and Substitutions for Turkish Lentil Soup

While the classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, there are ways to adapt it to your taste or dietary needs:

*   **Add Vegetables:** For extra nutrition and flavor, you can sauté finely diced carrots or potatoes along with the onions. They will cook down and blend seamlessly into the soup.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) to your preference. For a spicier kick, you can also add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Vegan Option:** This soup is naturally vegan if you use vegetable broth and olive oil instead of butter.
*   **Different Herbs:** While dried mint is classic, a touch of fresh dill or parsley stirred in at the end can add a different aromatic note.
*   **Thicker Consistency:** If you prefer a heartier soup, you can add a tablespoon or two of fine bulgur or rice along with the lentils. This will thicken the soup further, though it moves slightly away from the traditional smooth Mercimek Corbasi.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it’s an invitation to experience the warmth, generosity, and rich culinary heritage of Turkey. Simple to make, incredibly nourishing, and utterly delicious, this Turkish Red Lentil Soup is a dish that truly feeds the soul. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be transported to the vibrant kitchens of Turkey with every comforting spoonful.
